title: Harvest and Well
premise: Edmund Oyelaran, a skeptical property surveyor, arrives in the dying village of Harrow's Well to appraise Hollowmere House, only to find the house measuring her back—recording her heartbeat, her debts, her loneliness. The village founders, she learns, bound a harvest-god into the land with a ritual that requires a willing outsider every century, and the melted bell of 1911 rings to call a new one. As Edmund falls for the churchwarden's son, Tobias, who has spent his life preparing the next sacrifice, she must choose between escaping and completing the founders' unfinished rite—because an incomplete binding doesn't free the village, it lets the thing beneath the well finish feeding. In the end, Edmund rewrites the ritual itself, offering not her life but her belonging, becoming the house's new heart while Tobias breaks his family's duty; the bell falls silent, the village lives, and Edmund is never quite alone again.
about_author: Orsen Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural surveyor who spent six years cataloguing derelict properties across the English fenlands before turning to horror. Their debut novel draws on field notes from houses that were demolished before anyone could ask why no one ever bought them twice.

chapters.title: The Measurement Begins
chapters.summary: Edmund arrives in Harrow's Well to appraise Hollowmere House, finding rooms whose dimensions change between measurements and a ledger that lists her own name under 'prospective residents.' Her POV establishes her dry skepticism and professional detachment. Emotional beat: unease disguised as competence—the first crack in her certainty that everything can be surveyed.

chapters.title: A Village That Counts Its Guests
chapters.summary: In the pub, villagers greet Edmund by name though she told no one she was coming, and the landlord refuses payment, saying 'the house settles its own accounts.' Through Edmund's eyes we meet Tobias, the young churchwarden who watches her with something like pity. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of being expected—a stranger discovering she was invited.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't Cast
chapters.summary: At dawn the church bell rings, though parish records confirm it was melted down in 1911. Edmund investigates the empty belfry and finds fresh rope-wear on a beam older than the church itself. Her POV, rational explanations failing one by one. Emotional beat: the vertigo of evidence without explanation—her worldview's first real fracture.

chapters.title: Tobias at the Well
chapters.summary: Tobias finds Edmund sketching the covered well behind the house and warns her away with genuine fear rather than hostility. Over shared tea he reveals fragments: the founders, the covenant, the hundred-year arithmetic. His POV briefly takes over, showing his dread that she might be 'the one counted.' Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness between two people on opposite sides of a secret.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Alone overnight, Edmund experiences the house appraising her: mirrors showing her debts, walls warm where she grieves her dead mother, floorboards creaking in the rhythm of her childhood lullaby. She finds the founders' ritual chamber beneath the stairs, half-finished, waiting. Emotional beat: terror braided with terrible intimacy—the house knows her better than anyone living does.

chapters.title: The Founders' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Edmund researches in the parish archive: four disappearances, each one hundred years apart, each a lonely outsider who'd begun to belong. The last was 1911—the year the bell was melted, the ritual interrupted. Her POV, cold dread replacing skepticism. Emotional beat: the horror of pattern recognition—history isn't repeating, it's resuming.

chapters.title: Duty Is a Kind of Love
chapters.summary: Tobias confesses his inheritance: his family has been the churchwardens of the covenant for three centuries, raised to prepare the sacrifice and forbidden to love them. He begs her to leave before the solstice. His POV carries the chapter. Emotional beat: love against duty made flesh—he wants to save her by losing her.

chapters.title: The Well Breathes
chapters.summary: The cover stone over the well cracks. Livestock die facing it; crops ripen overnight, unnaturally fat. Villagers grow serene and welcoming in a way that chills Edmund more than hostility would. Her POV documents the land waking. Emotional beat: the corruption of comfort—belonging offered as bait.

chapters.title: Nineteen Eleven
chapters.summary: Edmund finds the diary of Ada Voss, the outsider of 1911, who fled mid-ritual when she learned what completion meant—and whose flight doomed the village to a slow century of decay. Ada's voice interleaves with Edmund's present. Emotional beat: kinship across a century—two women, same choice, different endings so far.

chapters.title: The Congregation of the Quiet
chapters.summary: The villagers hold a service for a bell that doesn't exist, singing harmonies to silence. Edmund attends and realizes they aren't deceived—they're complicit, fed small mercies by the thing below in exchange for the arrangement. Her POV. Emotional beat: moral nausea—she cannot hate people who are also victims, and victims who are also wardens.

chapters.title: What Tobias Was Built For
chapters.summary: Tobias shows Edmund the warden's ledger: generations of his family recording candidates, including his grandmother's note beside Edmund's name, written decades ago. He offers to burn the ledger and flee with her. His POV. Emotional beat: the temptation of escape—love proposing desertion, duty whispering the cost.

chapters.title: The House Makes Its Offer
chapters.summary: Hollowmere stops pretending: it shows Edmund a vision of her old life—empty flat, unread messages, a job that measures places without ever entering them—and then a vision of staying, warm and known forever. Her POV. Emotional beat: the seduction of power and belonging—the house doesn't threaten her, it recruits her.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Preparations begin openly: white cloths, the uncovered well, the villagers' faces slack with anticipation. Edmund tries to leave and finds the roads loop back to the village green no matter which way she drives. Her POV, panic sharpening into resolve. Emotional beat: the trap closing—invisibility was never an option; it never was for anyone.

chapters.title: Ada's Mistake
chapters.summary: Reading deeper into Ada's diary, Edmund discovers the ritual wasn't a sacrifice but a marriage—the god seeks a willing heart to anchor it, and Ada's flight left it starving and unbound. An incomplete rite means the thing rises free. Her POV. Emotional beat: reframing the horror—running isn't survival, it's apocalypse.

chapters.title: The Warden's Choice
chapters.summary: Tobias's father, the old churchwarden, catches them planning to break the covenant and reveals the family's true shame: they've been feeding candidates' names to the house for generations to spare their own children. His POV gives way to Tobias's fury and grief. Emotional beat: power's corruption inherited like blood—duty rotted into predation.

chapters.title: Beneath the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Edmund descends into the ritual chamber with Tobias and reads the founders' original words aloud; the house responds, walls breathing, the bell tolling underground. She feels the god's attention turn to her like a sunflower to light. Her POV. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve—she will not be chosen; she will choose.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: The village gathers for the eve-of rites, dressing Edmund in Ada's recovered gown whether she consents or not. Tobias defies his father publicly for the first time, and the congregation's serenity fractures into something hungry. Alternating POVs. Emotional beat: love against duty at open war—two people deciding, together, to rewrite a covenant.

chapters.title: The Rite Interrupted
chapters.summary: At the well at midnight, Edmund begins the ritual and deliberately diverges from the founders' script, speaking her own terms instead of submission. The ground splits; the thing beneath rises halfway, vast and patient and starving. Her POV inside the rite. Emotional beat: the climax's first movement—defiance as prayer, negotiation with the divine.

chapters.title: What Edmund Offers
chapters.summary: Edmund refuses both sacrifice and flight, offering instead her belonging—not her death but her permanence, her witness, her name kept by the house. Tobias joins his voice to hers, breaking the warden line's exclusive claim. The god considers. Her POV, transcendent and terrified. Emotional beat: the climax—love against duty resolved into a third covenant neither side scripted.

chapters.title: The Bell Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Dawn. The well closes over clean water; the house settles into stillness around Edmund, who can no longer quite leave it—or wants to. The villagers wake remembering nothing but a good harvest. Tobias stands in the doorway, unemployed by three centuries of duty. Shared POV. Emotional beat: aftermath's hush—victory that costs the shape of an ordinary life.

chapters.title: Appraisal
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Edmund files her report declaring Hollowmere structurally unsound and unfit for sale, ensuring no one else is ever sent. She and Tobias repair the house together, learning its moods, keeping its new heart company. Her POV. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than imposed—the quiet reward after the horror.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Line
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Edmund writes a final entry in the warden's ledger—not a candidate's name but a promise, and the house, for the first time, writes back a single word: home. Far away, another lonely surveyor receives an assignment in a village she's never heard of, and the last image holds. Her POV closing the frame. Emotional beat: peace shadowed by continuity—the covenant endures, changed, watching.
